messages.subject: using Ornstein-Uhlenbeck  model on INLA
parts:
Hi all,
I am interested in using the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model on INLA. I would like to know if you have some examples of how to fit that model and extract the parameters. 
In my case, I am interested on using it for phylogenetic analyses, that is: a graph with binary bifurcations and variable distances between the nodes, variables are only observed on the terminal nodes. The idea is to model the change of the variable over the graph allowing for different sections of the graph to have different rate of change and possibly direction of change.
I hope I have explained my self. A ref with a brief explanation of this is http://www2.hawaii.edu/~mbutler/PDFs/ButlerKing04.pdf

Look forward for your help and thanks very much in advance.
Best,

Inti Pedroso

On Thu, 2012-02-09 at 10:05 -0800, inti pedroso wrote:
> Hi all,
> I am interested in using the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model on INLA. I would
> like to know if you have some examples of how to fit that model and
> extract the parameters.
> In my case, I am interested on using it for phylogenetic analyses,
> that is: a graph with binary bifurcations and variable distances
> between the nodes, variables are only observed on the terminal nodes.
> The idea is to model the change of the variable over the graph
> allowing for different sections of the graph to have different rate of
> change and possibly direction of change.
> I hope I have explained my self. A ref with a brief explanation of
> this is http://www2.hawaii.edu/~mbutler/PDFs/ButlerKing04.pdf

This topic has been discussed in a post by
Julia Palacios from 27.january. I don't know if Finn or Dan has some
updates on this issue.

Anyway, you can use of the random-walk models, rw1 or rw2 (or crw2)
which is defined for irregular locations. Since the 'locations' is a bit
confusing sometimes, I've added a small example.

ps1: note that the prior for the rw-models is defined in an absolute
scale, with a typical distance between the locations of 1. so if you
scale the 'time' you need to change the prior.

ps2: if you have two locations to close, there can be a numerical
singularity and you get an error...

****************************


n = 100
interval = c(1, n)
x = seq(interval[1], interval[2], len = n)
ff = splinefun(x, sin(x/n * 4*pi))

## in the first case, we will have observations for all locations in the
## rw2 model at irregular locations

observation.locations = sort(runif(n, min=interval[1], max=interval[2]))
y = ff(observation.locations) + rnorm(n, sd=0.01)
r1 = inla(y ~ -1 + f(observation.locations, model="rw2", constr=FALSE),
data = data.frame(y, observation.locations))

## in the second case, we want to estimate the rw2 model with higher
## resultion, but we only have observations at
## 'observations.locations'. hence, we add the locations 1:n,
## additionally, to the rw2 model. this is done using the argument
## 'values'.

## these are the 'locations' for the rw2 model
values = unique(sort(c(1:n, observation.locations)))

## we need to pass these locations as argument 'values', otherwise,
## they are determined by the 'observation.locations' argument.

r2 = inla(y ~ -1 +
f(observation.locations, model="rw2",
values=values, constr=FALSE),
data = list(y=y, observation.locations=observation.locations,
values=values))

plot(r2$summary.random$observation.locations$ID,
r2$summary.random$observation.locations$mean, pch=1)
points(r1$summary.random$observation.locations$ID,
r1$summary.random$observation.locations$mean, pch=2)
